# Base guide {#sec-python-base-guide}

The lab's Python style is an amendment of
[Google's Python style guide](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/styleguide/blob/c03dfce4e1763d032e33696d126e5af4c7de03bf/pyguide.md),
read in the lab's fork at a pinned commit.
Follow that guide for everything the amendments below do not change.
Google's current wording is at
[google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html](https://google.github.io/styleguide/pyguide.html).

# Amendments {#sec-python-amendments}

## Linting and formatting with Ruff

[Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) replaces the pylint configuration and the Pyink formatter that Google's guide mentions.
It lints and formats in one tool.

- Lint settings live in the lab's `python/ruff.toml` in the `Morrison-Lab/psc` repository.
  Copy it to the root of a repository as `ruff.toml`.
- Line length stays at 80 characters, as in Google's guide.
- Docstrings follow Google's format.
- Rule families are pycodestyle, pyflakes, isort, pydocstyle, pyupgrade, bugbear, comprehensions and simplify.

CI runs the checks and fails on any finding.

## No nested function calls

The lab's [no-nested-calls rule](coding-style.qmd#sec-avoid-nesting) applies to Python.
Give each intermediate result a name.
Method chaining is fine.
Ruff cannot check this rule, so it is not yet enforced.

# Planned work {#sec-python-planned}

- Lint the Python chunks in `.qmd` files with the same configuration.
- Run the checks through `Morrison-Lab/gha`'s `check-python-package` workflow in every repository that contains Python.
- Open an issue when upstream changes Google's guide.

These are tracked in [#90](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/psc/issues/90).
